definition.def: A lecture is a talk someone gives in order to teach people about a particular subject, usually at a university or college.
examples: ...a series of lectures by Professor Eric Robinson. [+ by]
In his lecture Riemann covered an enormous variety of topics.

definition.def: If you lecture on a particular subject, you give a lecture or a series of lectures about it.
examples: She then invited him to Atlanta to lecture on the history of art. [V + on/in]
She has danced, choreographed, lectured and taught all over the world. [VERB]
Wendy Rigby was recently invited to lecture a group of doctors on the benefits of aromatherapy. [VERB noun on noun]

definition.def: If someone lectures you about something, they criticize you or tell you how they think you should behave.
examples: He used to lecture me about getting too much sun. [V n + about/on]
Chuck would lecture me, telling me to get a haircut. [VERB noun]
She was no longer interrogating but lecturing. [VERB]

examples.sentence: Inherently introverted, he realised early on that as an academic, his reticence would prove disastrous in the lecture hall.
And she also has a few $1,000 honoraria to offer in exchange for doctors' attendance at her company's next educational lecture.

If we think of a lecture we listened to with great concentration, we will recall the lecturer's appearance and mannerisms, our place in the auditorium, the failure of the air-conditioning, much more easily than the ideas we went to learn.
The details of the content of the lecture, on the other hand, seem to have gone forever.
Yours will be allocated at the first lecture.
A lecture is about an hour long, and a tutorial usually runs for about 2 hours.
A lecture is rather like what I'm doing now, where one person will talk to all of you together on a subject.
You are going to hear part of a public lecture for new students.
Uh. Good morning. Good morning everyone. And welcome to our regular lecture on health issues.
